note: One row per #[kani::proof] harness derived from source by scripts/p037_proof_boundary.py. `claim` restates only what the Kani body itself asserts (a proof/test twin sometimes asserts more or less; where that happens it is noted). `production_subject` quotes the kernel API the harness constrains, from its own doc comments where the source states one.

harnesses.claim: Transfer::join is commutative, associative, idempotent, has Bot as identity, and Unknown as an absorbing element.

Transfer::leq is reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive. (Its #[cfg(test)] twin additionally pins the height-3 facts -- No/Must incomparable, Bot<=No<=May<=Unknown -- which this Kani proof does not itself assert.)
Cells::join is commutative, associative, idempotent, with Cells::BOT as identity.
Election::join is commutative, associative, idempotent, has None as identity, and Conflict as an absorbing element.
Cells::collapse is monotone w.r.t. leq, is a join-morphism, and Cells::diag(t).collapse() == t.
import(e1,binding) <= import(e2,binding) whenever e1 <= e2; import(Conflict,*) = Conflict; import(None,*) = None.
ElectionSystem::step(i,x) <= ElectionSystem::step(i,y) at every coordinate i, given x <= y pointwise.
elect(sys) terminates within the height bound, is a fixpoint of sys.step, and is <= every other fixpoint (the least fixpoint).
On a 2-coordinate election system with <=1 edge each, elect_with(sys, schedule) under any fair schedule equals elect(sys), when both terminate.
harnesses.production_subject: elect_with() vs elect() (election lfp, chaotic schedule)

harnesses.claim: read(t,.) and contribute(m, read(t,.)) are monotone in the cell argument; every component of read(t,c) is <= c.collapse(), and contribute only lowers further. (Merges the two differently-named #[cfg(test)] twins k3_reads_and_contributions_are_monotone and k3_every_read_component_is_below_the_collapse into one body.)
harnesses.production_subject: read() (G-F2) and contribute() (G-S4 applied to a G-F2 read)

harnesses.claim: read(Id,.) and read(Neg,.) are involutions; read(Neg,c) == c.swap(); read(Opaque,.), read(ConstPos,.), read(ConstNeg,.) always produce a diagonal Cells.
harnesses.production_subject: read() with Transform::{Id,Neg,Opaque,ConstPos,ConstNeg} (the five G-S5 edge transforms)

harnesses.claim: From a symbolic state whose Uncond-shaped coordinates already hold diagonal Cells, one application of System::step to an Uncond coordinate again yields a diagonal Cells (the inductive step).
On a 2-coordinate system, solve(sys) keeps every Uncond-shaped coordinate's Cells diagonal.
System::step(i,x) <= System::step(i,y) at every coordinate i, given x <= y pointwise. (Fact (a) of the module's 3-lemma schedule-independence decomposition.)
solve(sys) terminates within the height bound, is a fixpoint of sys.step, and is <= every other fixpoint. (Fact (b).)
On a 2-coordinate system, solve_with(sys, schedule) under any fair schedule equals solve(sys), when both terminate. (Fact (c); K10 is the name lib.rs itself gives this order-independence property.)
For an arbitrary Grounding g (restricted, for PartialLocalRelease(t), to t in {Must, May}): lemma_guarded(g).fin().collapse() <= lemma_today(g).fin().

For a symbolic well-formed 3-coordinate System and symbolic state x: collapsing one step of the guarded solver is <= one step of the fully-collapsed system on the collapsed state, at every coordinate (the G-T2 §7.2 induction step).
On a 2-coordinate system, collapse(solve(sys)) <= collapse(solve(sys.collapsed())) coordinatewise, pre-finalization (G-T2a at the lfp level).

On a 2-coordinate system whose cell-local release facts are consistent, the finalized-and-collapsed guarded lfp is, at every live coordinate, either <= the finalized-and-collapsed lfp of System::today(), or exactly (Unknown, May) (G-T2b as amended).
harnesses.production_subject: solve(sys) vs solve(sys.today()) -- System::today models ownlang/ownir.py's _build_skeletons derivation ladder

harnesses.claim: On a 2-coordinate system with consistent cell-local release facts AND no coordinate seeding Unknown, the finalized-and-collapsed guarded lfp is <= the finalized-and-collapsed lfp of System::today() (G-T2 as originally stated, pre-K11b-amendment; retained as the historical un-amended claim, superseded by K11b for the general case).

apply(shape,c,sel) lowers to Consume exactly when either the statically-selected finalized cell is Must, or both finalized cells are unanimously Must; for Uncond, apply ignores the selection (the G-A2 floor).

apply/lower never produce Consume when the finalized cells disagree or the selected finalized cell is Unknown; a raw Bot finalizes to Borrow; and applying the UNfinalized pair (Must,Bot) yields Plain because apply finalizes before it selects or collapses (the unfinalized-read witness -- a raw solver cell is never consumable).

not_kani_proved_test_only.note: K13 ('the worked rows of P-037 §8') and three refinement.rs row/finding functions exist only as #[cfg(test)] functions with no Kani twin: row1_teardown_skip, row3_dispose_bool_misplaced_release, rows7_8_wrapper_inherits_the_split_through_id_and_neg, row9_alternating_recursion_is_unanimous_must, rows12_13_mixed_release_forward_consumes_without_selection, row14_one_cell_residual_bottom, row16_forward_grounded_residual_bottom, row17_none_coordinate_refined_through_const_pos, row18_mutated_guard_degrades_to_opaque (application.rs), row11_late_conflict_cannot_leave_a_stale_import, k11_finding_release_priority_drops_an_unresolved_forward (election.rs/refinement.rs). This is a real, named asymmetry between 'tested' and 'Kani-proved' -- not a defect in the audit, since §10.4 only requires deriving the Kani inventory, but worth carrying forward rather than letting the word 'harness' quietly cover both.
